messages.subject: Re: mapqtl file format for r/qtl
messages.body_plain:
With the mapqtl format, I think R/qtl requires that the genotypes for a marker (in the .loc file) be all on one line, rather than split over multiple lines. This is likely the cause of the error you are seeing.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL effect p value
messages.body_plain:
The LOD score is equivalent to a t-test. The approach we take for p-values is to use a permutation test, particularly so that we can then adjust for the scan across the genome. And so I would focus on genome-scan-adjusted p-values that you can get from the scanone summary.

the t-value with estimated effects in fitqtl() would just be estimate / SE, and the p-values do not adjust for the genome scan. I ignore those p-values completely.

karl

messages.subject: calcerror.lod Vs calc.genoprob
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am creating a linkage map from whole-genome sequencing data.
For the subsetted SNP dataset of a chromosome, calcerror.lod() can point out potential errors.
But if I pass the complete SNP data of the same chromosome, it just says "no cutoffs above error lods". As a result, I cannot clean the data and I see lots of errors in the output.

you said you yourself use calc.genoprob instead of calcerror.lod
but I am not sure how that solves the issue.

I was using calc.errorlod() as follows:
# Identify problematic markers based on crossovers
hcsnpssr <- calc.errorlod(hcsnpssr, error.prob=0.0001, map.function=c("kosambi"))
# Identify marker genotypes with a large LOD score.
(toperr5 <- top.errorlod(hcsnpssr, cutoff=5,msg=TRUE))
totmar(hcsnpssr)
tab<- table(toperr5[,3])
drop1<- names(tab[tab>=3])
totmar(hcsnpssr)
hcsnpssr <- drop.markers(hcsnpssr, drop1)
totmar(hcsnpssr)

messages.subject: Re: Scanone VS Scantwo
messages.body_plain:
It's not really a matter of reliability. scanone() fits a single-QTL model at each position, while scantwo() fits a two-QTL model. The estimated location of QTL may depend on whether you're including other QTL in the model.

karl

messages.subject: LOD support interval does not match expected 1.5-drop LOD value
messages.subject_clean: LOD support interval does not match expected 1.5-drop LOD value
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am attempting to obtain the LOD support interval using function 'lodint'. My peak LOD value for the chromosome is 5.1, so I would expect the support interval to include markers of LOD 3.6 or higher (if I interpret correctly the meaning of a 1.5-drop LOD score...). When I perform the 'lodint' function, I obtain flanking markers of 3.32 and 2.80 LOD at either end of the QTL region, which is a lower threshold than I would anticipate based on my QTL peak value.

I have included my code below. [Sidenote* My QTL plots include an LOD threshold line of 3.91, as that was the significance value obtained after 1000 permutations testing].

Thank you for any insights you could provide!

Cheers,
David

#CIM for trait
out1_cim.em <- cim(mapthis, pheno.col = (1), n.marcovar=1, method=c("em"), map.function=c("kosambi"))

#Regression for trait
summary(out1_cim.em, threshold=3.91)
mapthis <- sim.geno(mapthis, n.draws=128)
qtl_traitA_avg_chr1 <- makeqtl(mapthis, chr=c(1), pos=c(213))
summary(out.qtl_traitA_avg_chr1 <- fitqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, pheno.col=1, formula=y~Q1))
plot(qtl_traitA_avg_chr1)

#fit the model (with QTL in fixed positions)
out.fq_traitA_avg_chr1 <- fitqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, formula=y~Q1)
summary(out.fq_traitA_avg_chr1)

#refine QTL and plot LOD profile
rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1 <- refineqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, formula=y~Q1, verbose=FALSE)
rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1
out.fq2_traitA_avg_chr1 <- fitqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, formula=y~Q1, dropone=FALSE)
summary(out.fq2_traitA_avg_chr1)
plotLodProfile(rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1)
abline(3.91, 0, untf = FALSE)
title(main = "Trait A")

#obtain LOD support interval
lodint(rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1, chr, qtl.index=1, drop=1.5, lodcolumn=1, expandtomarkers=FALSE)

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] LOD support interval does not match expected 1.5-drop LOD value
messages.body_plain:
The endpoints of the support interval that lodint (with drop=1.5) calculates are the left- and right-most positions on the chromosome where the LOD score is within 1.5 of the maximum. If there are multiple peaks, they all get merged together.

karl
